SYNTHETIC DATA. Case PR-2026-0205, resolved 12 Feb 2026 by R. Menon (Procurement Ops). Kind: experience.
Failed checks: budget (cause: overrun).
Request: ₹1,60,000 direct material, spindle motor spares, vendor V-041, urgency line_down.
What happened: line 2 stopped on a failed spindle; cost centre CC-MACH was 5% over its annual budget after this order.
Why the standard process did not fit: the budget check blocks the order, but the line was down and the overrun was small (5%).
Steps approved (codes): ALLOW_BUDGET_OVERRUN, ATTACH_LINE_DOWN_EVIDENCE, ADD_CONTROLLER_SIGNOFF, EXPEDITE_PO.
Outcome: line restarted the next day; controller approved the overrun.
Lesson: an emergency overrun of up to 10% with the line down is allowed with line-down evidence and controller sign-off.

metadata.outcome: line restarted the next day; controller approved the overrun.

SYNTHETIC DATA. Case PR-2026-0233, resolved 20 Feb 2026 by R. Menon (Procurement Ops). Kind: experience.
Failed checks: bank (cause: bank_details_changed).
Request: ₹3,20,000 direct material, forged steel blanks, vendor V-031, urgency normal.
What happened: vendor V-031 changed its bank account 9 days before the request, by email.
Why the standard process did not fit: the bank check only flags the change; it says nothing about whether the change is genuine, and a changed account is a classic payment-fraud route.
Steps approved (codes): VERIFY_BANK_CALLBACK, HOLD_PAYMENT, HOLD_PO.
Outcome: callback to the number on file confirmed the new account; PO released after 2 days.
Lesson: a recent bank change means a callback on a known number and a payment hold before anything else.

metadata.outcome: callback to the number on file confirmed the new account; PO released after 2 days.

SYNTHETIC DATA. Case PR-2026-0266, resolved 26 Feb 2026 by R. Menon (Procurement Ops). Kind: experience.
Failed checks: duplicate (cause: possible_duplicate).
Request: ₹75,000 indirect mro, packaging crates, second shipment, vendor V-050, urgency normal.
What happened: a request 3% off an earlier one to the same vendor two weeks before; it was the second shipment of the same order, split by the vendor.
Why the standard process did not fit: the duplicate check flags a split shipment as a duplicate order.
Steps approved (codes): LINK_MASTER_PO, ALLOW_SPLIT_DELIVERY.
Outcome: linked to the master PO; no double payment.
Lesson: a split shipment of one order is linked to its master PO, not rejected as a duplicate, when the vendor has no duplicate-invoice history.

metadata.outcome: linked to the master PO; no double payment.

SYNTHETIC DATA. Case PR-2026-0312, resolved 11 Mar 2026 by R. Menon (Procurement Ops). Kind: interaction.
Failed checks: bank (cause: bank_details_changed) + budget (cause: overrun).
Request: ₹1,85,000 direct material, coolant pump assemblies, vendor V-031, urgency line_down.
What happened: line 3 stopped; V-031 changed bank details 12 days earlier; CC-MACH 7% over budget.
Why the standard process did not fit: the plain combination holds the PO until the bank callback, which would have kept line 3 down; a PO is not a payment.
Plain combination would have been: VERIFY_BANK_CALLBACK, HOLD_PAYMENT, HOLD_PO, ALLOW_BUDGET_OVERRUN, ATTACH_LINE_DOWN_EVIDENCE, ADD_CONTROLLER_SIGNOFF, EXPEDITE_PO.
Steps approved (codes): EXPEDITE_PO, VERIFY_BANK_CALLBACK, HOLD_PAYMENT, ALLOW_BUDGET_OVERRUN, ATTACH_LINE_DOWN_EVIDENCE, ADD_CONTROLLER_SIGNOFF.
Removed from the plain combination: HOLD_PO, because the PO was released while payment stayed held until the callback.
Outcome: parts arrived next day; callback confirmed the account; payment released after controller sign-off.
Lesson: when a bank change meets a line-down overrun, release the PO but hold the payment until the callback.

metadata.outcome: parts arrived next day; callback confirmed the account; payment released after controller sign-off.

SYNTHETIC DATA. Case PR-2026-0417, resolved 14 Mar 2026 by R. Menon (Procurement Ops). Kind: experience.
Failed checks: vendor (cause: cert_expired).
Request: ₹1,40,000 direct material, bearing housings, vendor V-017, urgency normal.
What happened: ISO 9001 certificate expired 6 days before the request; vendor V-017 has 2 years of on-time delivery.
Why the standard process did not fit: the vendor check blocks the vendor outright, but the vendor was otherwise in good standing and renewal was in progress.
Steps approved (codes): REQUEST_RENEWED_CERT, KEEP_VENDOR_ACTIVE, HOLD_PO.
Outcome: renewed certificate received in 3 days; PO released.
Lesson: a recently expired certificate is a hold, not a rejection, when the vendor is otherwise in good standing.

SYNTHETIC DATA. Case PR-2026-0360, resolved 24 Mar 2026 by R. Menon (Procurement Ops). Kind: interaction.
Failed checks: approver (cause: approver_on_leave) + budget (cause: overrun).
Request: ₹1,70,000 direct material, gearbox bearings, vendor V-044, urgency line_down.
What happened: line 1 down; CC-MACH 6% over budget; approver E-104 on leave with delegate E-112 up to ₹2,00,000.
Why the standard process did not fit: delegates don't approve budget overruns, even within their limit, so routing to the delegate would have stalled.
Plain combination would have been: ROUTE_DELEGATE, ALLOW_BUDGET_OVERRUN, ATTACH_LINE_DOWN_EVIDENCE, ADD_CONTROLLER_SIGNOFF, EXPEDITE_PO.
Steps approved (codes): ROUTE_NEXT_LEVEL_APPROVER, ADD_CONTROLLER_SIGNOFF, ALLOW_BUDGET_OVERRUN, ATTACH_LINE_DOWN_EVIDENCE, EXPEDITE_PO.
Removed from the plain combination: ROUTE_DELEGATE, because a delegate may not approve an overrun; routed to the next-level approver instead.
Outcome: plant head approved within hours; line restarted next day.
Lesson: when the approver is away and the budget overruns, route to the next-level approver, not the delegate.

metadata.outcome: plant head approved within hours; line restarted next day.

SYNTHETIC DATA. Case PR-2026-0720, resolved 06 Aug 2026 by R. Menon (Procurement Ops). Kind: experience.
Failed checks: approver (cause: approver_on_leave).
Request: ₹4,20,000 capex, a bench grinder (capex), vendor V-030, urgency normal.
What happened: the approver was on leave; the delegation was valid; the request was capex, after the 1 Jul 2026 policy memo.
Why the standard process did not fit: the approver was away; under the 1 Jul 2026 memo a capex delegate approval needs Finance Controller co-sign.
Steps approved (codes): ROUTE_DELEGATE, ADD_CONTROLLER_SIGNOFF.
Outcome: delegate approved with controller co-sign.
Lesson: since 1 Jul 2026, capex approved by a delegate also needs the Finance Controller's co-sign.
